Q1: Farnesol has known acute and chronic environmental hazards. While there is an expanded perspective on potential endocrine disruption, and dermal and eye hazards, data are deficient for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive, inhalation, and organ/systemic hazards. Oral hazards are considered to be of low to moderate concern.
Q2: Farnesol is not found on any lists of concern but is recognized as an EPA "Substance Added to Food." This suggests it is generally considered of low concern in regulated applications.
Q3: Farnesol is a well-defined small molecule with over 6,800 scientific literature references, indicating extensive study. It also has 43 toxicity records, reflecting a moderate level of toxicological investigation, although its carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive, inhalation, and organ/systemic hazards remain data deficient.
